title_en: Anti-Monopoly Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is formulated for the purposes of preventing and restraining monopolistic conduct, protecting fair competition in the market, encouraging innovation, improving economic efficiency, safeguarding consumer interests and public interest, and promoting the healthy development of the socialist market economy.

Article 2 This Law shall apply to monopolistic conduct in economic activities within the territory of the People's Republic of China; monopolistic conduct outside the territory of the People's Republic of China that has the effect of eliminating or restricting competition in the domestic market shall be governed by this Law.

Article 4 The anti-monopoly work shall adhere to the leadership of the Communist Party of China.
The State shall adhere to the principles of marketization and rule of law, strengthen the fundamental role of competition policies, formulate and implement competition rules compatible with the socialist market economy, improve macro-control, and establish a unified, open, competitive, and orderly market system.

Article 5 The State shall establish and improve the fair competition review system.
Administrative organs and organizations authorized by laws or regulations to have the function of managing public affairs shall conduct a fair competition review when formulating regulations involving the economic activities of market entities.

Article 6 Business operators may, through fair competition and voluntary association, implement concentration in accordance with law, expand their business scale, and enhance their market competitiveness.
Article 7 A business operator with a dominant market position shall not abuse its dominant market position to eliminate or restrict competition.

Article 8 For industries that are under the control of the state-owned economy and related to the lifeline of the national economy and national security, as well as industries that implement franchising or monopoly sales according to law, the State shall protect the lawful business activities of business operators in these industries, and shall supervise and regulate their business conduct and the prices of their goods and services in accordance with law, safeguard consumer interests, and promote technological progress.
Business operators in the industries mentioned in the preceding paragraph shall operate in accordance with law, be honest and trustworthy, exercise strict self-discipline, accept supervision from the public, and shall not use their control position or franchising/monopoly sales position to harm consumer interests.
Article 9 Business operators shall not use data, algorithms, technology, capital advantages, or platform rules to engage in monopolistic conduct prohibited by this Law.

Article 10 Administrative organs and organizations authorized by laws or regulations to have the function of managing public affairs shall not abuse administrative power to eliminate or restrict competition.

Article 11 The State shall improve and perfect the anti-monopoly rules and institutions, strengthen anti-monopoly regulatory forces, enhance the modernization level of regulatory capabilities and regulatory systems, strengthen anti-monopoly law enforcement and justice, handle monopoly cases in accordance with law fairly and efficiently, improve the mechanism for linking administrative law enforcement with justice, and maintain a fair competition order.

Article 13 The anti-monopoly law enforcement agency under the State Council shall be responsible for the unified anti-monopoly law enforcement work.
The anti-monopoly law enforcement agency under the State Council may, as needed for work, authorize the corresponding agencies of the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, or municipalities directly under the Central Government to be responsible for relevant anti-monopoly law enforcement work in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

Article 14 Trade associations shall strengthen self-discipline in their industries, guide business operators in their industries to compete in accordance with law, operate in compliance, and maintain the order of market competition.

Article 15 For the purposes of this Law, "business operator" means a natural person, legal person, or unincorporated organization that engages in the production, operation, or provision of services.
For the purposes of this Law, "relevant market" means the scope of goods and the geographical scope within which business operators compete for specific goods or services (hereinafter collectively referred to as goods) during a certain period.
Article 16 For the purposes of this Law, "monopoly agreement" means an agreement, decision, or other concerted conduct that eliminates or restricts competition.
Article 19 Business operators shall not organize other business operators to reach monopoly agreements or provide substantive assistance to other business operators in reaching monopoly agreements.
Article 21 Trade associations shall not organize business operators in their industry to engage in monopolistic conduct prohibited under this Chapter.

Article 26 Where a concentration of business operators reaches the notification threshold prescribed by the State Council, a business operator shall file a prior notification with the anti-monopoly enforcement authority under the State Council; if no notification is filed, the concentration shall not be implemented.
Where a concentration of business operators does not reach the notification threshold prescribed by the State Council, but there is evidence that the concentration has or may have the effect of eliminating or restricting competition, the anti-monopoly enforcement authority under the State Council may require the business operator to file a notification.
Where a business operator fails to file a notification in accordance with the preceding two paragraphs, the anti-monopoly enforcement authority under the State Council shall conduct an investigation according to law.

Article 29 Where the documents and materials submitted by a business operator are incomplete, the business operator shall supplement them within the time limit prescribed by the anti-monopoly enforcement authority under the State Council. If the business operator fails to supplement them within the time limit, it shall be deemed not to have filed a notification.

Article 30 The anti-monopoly enforcement authority under the State Council shall, within thirty days from the date of receipt of the documents and materials submitted by the business operator that comply with the provisions of Article 28 of this Law, conduct a preliminary review of the notified concentration, make a decision on whether to conduct further review, and inform the business operator in writing. Before the anti-monopoly enforcement authority under the State Council makes a decision, the business operator shall not implement the concentration.
If the anti-monopoly enforcement authority under the State Council decides not to conduct further review or fails to make a decision within the time limit, the business operator may implement the concentration.

Article 34 Where a concentration of business operators has or may have the effect of eliminating or restricting competition, the anti-monopoly enforcement authority under the State Council shall make a decision to prohibit the concentration. However, if the business operator can demonstrate that the beneficial effects of the concentration on competition clearly outweigh its adverse effects, or that the concentration is in the public interest, the anti-monopoly enforcement authority under the State Council may decide not to prohibit the concentration.

Article 35 For a concentration that is not prohibited, the anti-monopoly enforcement authority under the State Council may decide to impose restrictive conditions to reduce the adverse effects of the concentration on competition.

Article 36 The anti-monopoly enforcement authority under the State Council shall promptly announce to the public its decision to prohibit a concentration or a decision to impose restrictive conditions on a concentration.

Article 37 The anti-monopoly enforcement authority under the State Council shall improve the classification and hierarchical review system for concentrations of business operators, strengthen the review of concentrations in important fields such as those affecting the national economy and public livelihood according to law, and improve the quality and efficiency of review.

Article 38 Where foreign investors acquire domestic enterprises or participate in concentrations of business operators in other ways that involve national security, a national security review shall be conducted in accordance with the relevant provisions of the state, in addition to the review of the concentration under this Law.

Article 39 Administrative organs and organizations authorized by laws or regulations to have functions of managing public affairs shall not abuse their administrative power to restrict or restrict in disguised form entities or individuals from operating, purchasing, or using products provided by designated business operators.

Article 40 Administrative organs and organizations authorized by laws or regulations to have functions of managing public affairs shall not abuse their administrative power to impede other business operators from entering the relevant market or to impose unequal treatment on other business operators by entering into cooperation agreements, memorandums, or other means, thereby eliminating or restricting competition.

Article 42 An administrative organ or an organization authorized by law or regulation to perform functions of public affairs administration shall not abuse its administrative power to exclude or restrict business operators from participating in tenders, bidding, or other business activities by means such as setting discriminatory qualification requirements, evaluation standards, or failing to release information according to law.

Article 43 An administrative organ or an organization authorized by law or regulation to perform functions of public affairs administration shall not abuse its administrative power to exclude, restrict, compel, or constructively compel business operators from other regions to invest or set up branch offices in the local area by means such as unequal treatment compared to local business operators.

Article 44 An administrative organ or an organization authorized by law or regulation to perform functions of public affairs administration shall not abuse its administrative power to compel or constructively compel business operators to engage in monopolistic conducts as prescribed by this Law.

Article 45 An administrative organ or an organization authorized by law or regulation to perform functions of public affairs administration shall not abuse its administrative power to formulate provisions containing contents that exclude or restrict competition.

Article 46 The anti-monopoly law enforcement agency shall investigate suspected monopolistic conducts according to law.
Any entity or individual has the right to report suspected monopolistic conducts to the anti-monopoly law enforcement agency. The anti-monopoly law enforcement agency shall keep the reporter confidential.
If the report is in written form and provides relevant facts and evidence, the anti-monopoly law enforcement agency shall conduct a necessary investigation.

Article 48 When the anti-monopoly law enforcement agency investigates suspected monopolistic conducts, there shall be no fewer than two law enforcement officers, and they shall present their law enforcement credentials.
Law enforcement officers shall make records when conducting inquiries and investigations, and such records shall be signed by the persons being inquired or investigated.

Article 49 The anti-monopoly law enforcement agency and its staff members shall bear the obligation of confidentiality according to law with respect to trade secrets, personal privacy, and personal information learned in the course of law enforcement.

Article 50 The business operator under investigation, interested parties, or other relevant entities or individuals shall cooperate with the anti-monopoly law enforcement agency in its performance of duties according to law, and shall not refuse or obstruct the investigations of the anti-monopoly law enforcement agency.

Article 51 The business operator under investigation and interested parties have the right to state their opinions. The anti-monopoly law enforcement agency shall verify the facts, reasons, and evidence provided by the business operator under investigation and interested parties.

Article 52 After investigation and verification, if the anti-monopoly law enforcement agency determines that a suspected monopolistic conduct constitutes a monopolistic conduct, it shall make a handling decision according to law and may make it public.

Article 53 For a suspected monopolistic conduct under investigation by the anti-monopoly law enforcement agency, if the business operator under investigation undertakes to take specific measures within a time limit acceptable to the anti-monopoly law enforcement agency to eliminate the consequences of such conduct, the anti-monopoly law enforcement agency may decide to suspend the investigation. The decision to suspend the investigation shall specify the detailed contents of the business operator's undertaking.
If the anti-monopoly law enforcement agency decides to suspend the investigation, it shall supervise the business operator's performance of the undertaking. If the business operator performs the undertaking, the anti-monopoly law enforcement agency may decide to terminate the investigation.
The anti-monopoly law enforcement agency shall resume the investigation under any of the following circumstances:
(1) The business operator fails to perform its undertaking;
(2) The facts on which the decision to suspend the investigation was based have undergone material changes; or
(3) The decision to suspend the investigation was made based on incomplete or untrue information provided by the business operator.

Article 54 The anti-monopoly law enforcement agency shall investigate, according to law, suspected conducts of abusing administrative power to exclude or restrict competition, and relevant entities or individuals shall cooperate.

Article 55 If a business operator, an administrative organ, or an organization authorized by law or regulation to perform functions of public affairs administration is suspected of violating the provisions of this Law, the anti-monopoly law enforcement agency may conduct an interview with its legal representative or responsible person, and require it to propose improvement measures.

Article 56 Where a business operator, in violation of the provisions of this Law, concludes and implements a monopoly agreement, the anti-monopoly law enforcement agency shall order it to cease the illegal act, confiscate its illegal gains, and concurrently impose a fine of not less than 1% but not more than 10% of its sales revenue in the preceding year; if there is no sales revenue in the preceding year, a fine of not more than RMB 5 million yuan shall be imposed. Where a monopoly agreement that has been concluded is not implemented, a fine of not more than RMB 3 million yuan may be imposed. The legal representative, principal responsible person, and directly responsible persons of the business operator who bear personal responsibility for concluding the monopoly agreement may be imposed a fine of not more than RMB 1 million yuan.
Where a business operator organizes other business operators to conclude a monopoly agreement or provides substantial assistance to other business operators in concluding a monopoly agreement, the preceding paragraph shall apply.
Where a business operator voluntarily reports to the anti-monopoly law enforcement agency the relevant circumstances of concluding a monopoly agreement and provides material evidence, the anti-monopoly law enforcement agency may, at its discretion, mitigate or exempt the penalty on such business operator.
Where a trade association, in violation of the provisions of this Law, organizes the business operators in its industry to conclude a monopoly agreement, the anti-monopoly law enforcement agency shall order it to make corrections, and may impose a fine of not more than RMB 3 million yuan; if the circumstances are serious, the registration and management authority for social organizations may revoke its registration according to law.

Article 57 Where a business operator, in violation of the provisions of this Law, abuses a dominant market position, the anti-monopoly law enforcement agency shall order it to cease the illegal act, confiscate its illegal gains, and concurrently impose a fine of not less than 1% but not more than 10% of its sales revenue in the preceding year.

Article 58 Where a business operator implements a concentration in violation of the provisions of this Law, and such concentration has or may have the effect of excluding or restricting competition, the anti-monopoly law enforcement agency under the State Council shall order it to cease implementing the concentration, dispose of shares or assets within a time limit, transfer business within a time limit, and take other necessary measures to restore the status quo ante of the concentration, and impose a fine of not more than 10% of its sales revenue in the preceding year; if the concentration does not have the effect of excluding or restricting competition, a fine of not more than RMB 5 million yuan shall be imposed.

Article 59 For the fines prescribed in Articles 56, 57, and 58 of this Law, the anti-monopoly law enforcement agency, when determining the specific amount of the fine, shall take into account factors such as the nature, severity, and duration of the illegal act, and the circumstances of eliminating the consequences of the illegal act.

Article 60 Where a business operator engages in monopolistic conduct and causes losses to others, it shall bear civil liability according to law.
Where a business operator engages in monopolistic conduct and damages the public interest, the People's Procuratorate at or above the level of a districted city may, according to law, institute a civil public interest action with the People's Court.

Article 61 Where an administrative organ or an organization authorized by laws or regulations to have the function of managing public affairs abuses administrative powers to eliminate or restrict competition, the superior organ shall order it to make corrections; the persons directly in charge and other persons directly responsible shall be given sanctions according to law. The anti-monopoly enforcement agency may propose to the relevant superior organ to handle the matter according to law. The administrative organ or the organization authorized by laws or regulations to have the function of managing public affairs shall report the correction in writing to the superior organ and the anti-monopoly enforcement agency.
Where laws or administrative regulations provide otherwise on the handling of the abuse of administrative power by an administrative organ or an organization authorized by laws or regulations to have the function of managing public affairs to eliminate or restrict competition, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 62 Where anyone refuses to provide relevant materials or information, or provides false materials or information, or conceals, destroys, or transfers evidence, or commits any other act of refusing or obstructing the review or investigation conducted by the anti-monopoly enforcement agency according to law, the anti-monopoly enforcement agency shall order it to make corrections, and impose a fine of not more than one percent of the sales revenue of the preceding year on the entity, or where there is no sales revenue in the preceding year or the sales revenue is difficult to calculate, impose a fine of not more than five million yuan; and impose a fine of not more than five hundred thousand yuan on the individual.

Article 63 Where the violation of the provisions of this Law is of a particularly serious nature, has an especially adverse impact, or causes especially serious consequences, the anti-monopoly enforcement agency under the State Council may determine the specific amount of the fine at not less than two times but not more than five times the amount of the fine prescribed in Articles 56, 57, 58 and 62 of this Law.

Article 64 Where an business operator is subject to an administrative penalty for violating the provisions of this Law, it shall be recorded in the credit record in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State and be publicized to the society.

Article 65 Where a party is dissatisfied with a decision made by the anti-monopoly enforcement agency pursuant to Articles 34 and 35 of this Law, it may first apply for administrative reconsideration according to law; if it is dissatisfied with the decision of administrative reconsideration, it may institute an administrative action according to law.
Where a party is dissatisfied with a decision made by the anti-monopoly enforcement agency other than those specified in the preceding paragraph, it may apply for administrative reconsideration or institute an administrative action according to law.

Article 66 Where a staff member of the anti-monopoly enforcement agency abuses his or her power, neglects his or her duty, commits malpractice for personal gain, or divulges trade secrets, personal privacy or personal information known during the enforcement process, he or she shall be given a sanction according to law.
Article 67 Where a violation of the provisions of this Law constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 68 This Law shall not apply to the exercise of intellectual property rights by business operators in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations on intellectual property; however, this Law shall apply to the abuse of intellectual property rights by business operators to eliminate or restrict competition.

Article 69 This Law shall not apply to the joint or concerted conduct of agricultural producers and rural economic organizations in the production, processing, sales, transportation, storage and other business activities of agricultural products.
Article 70 This Law shall come into force as of August 1, 2008.
